targets.quote: 1.   The yearly average GHG intensity of the energy used on board by a ship during a reporting period shall not exceed the limit set out in paragraph 2.
targets.article: Article 4(1) — GHG intensity limit on energy used on board by a ship
targets.label: target
indicators: yearly average GHG intensity of energy used on board

targets.quote: 2.   The limit referred to in paragraph 1 shall be calculated by reducing the reference value of 91,16 grams of CO2 equivalent per MJ by the following percentage:
targets.label: target

targets.quote: 1.   For the calculation of the GHG intensity of the energy used on board by a ship, from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2033 a multiplier of ‘2’ can be used to reward the ship for the use of RFNBO. The methodology for this calculation is set out in Annex I.
targets.article: Article 5(1) — Use of Renewable Fuels of Non-Biological Origin
targets.label: other
indicators: GHG intensity of energy used on board

targets.quote: 3.   If the share of RFNBO referred to in paragraph 2 is less than 1 % for the reporting period 2031, a subtarget of 2 % shall apply for such fuels in the yearly energy used on board by a ship from 1 January 2034, subject to paragraph 5.
targets.label: target
indicators: share of RFNBO in yearly energy used on board (subtarget %)

targets.quote: 1.   From 1 January 2030, a ship moored at the quayside in a port of call which is covered by Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 and which is under the jurisdiction of a Member State shall connect to OPS and use it for all its electrical power demand at berth.
targets.article: Article 6(1) — Additional zero-emission requirements for energy used at berth
targets.label: obligation
indicators: on-shore power supply (OPS) connection at berth

targets.quote: 2.   From 1 January 2035, a ship moored at the quayside in a port of call which is not covered by Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804, which is under the jurisdiction of a Member State and where the quay is equipped with available OPS shall connect to that OPS and use it for all its electrical power demand at berth.
targets.label: obligation
indicators: on-shore power supply (OPS) connection at berth
